CoreCSharp11AsyncThreadMegaStress.cs
====================================

Purpose
-------
Positive/runnable stress fixture for compiler and runtime testing of C# async/await,
threading, synchronization, concurrency, and their interaction with core C# language
features through C# 11.

Source rules
------------
- No `using` directives.
- Global `printf(...)` is assumed to be a compiler/runtime intrinsic.
- Fully-qualified framework type names are used where runtime threading/task types are required.
- `using (...)` statements and `await using` are intentionally present; these are statements,
  not `using` directives, and are themselves language features under test.
- Unsafe compilation must be enabled for the unsafe/function-pointer section.
- Target language version: C# 11.
- Dynamic binding is intentionally exercised.

Output format
-------------
The source uses pipe-delimited records intended for automated parsing.

TRACE|order=ORDERED|area=<area>|test=<test>|event=<event>|key=value|...
    Deterministic/control-flow trace. Compare sequence where the named test is ordered.

CONCURRENT|order=UNORDERED|area=<area>|test=<test>|logicalId=<id>|event=<event>|...
    Concurrent trace. Validate the expected set/multiset of records by logical IDs and fields;
    do not require scheduler-dependent line ordering.

RACE|order=UNORDERED|area=<area>|test=<test>|comparison=NONDETERMINISTIC|...
    Intentional data-race test. Validate bounds/invariants and presence, not an exact final value.

FINALIZER|order=UNORDERED|type=<type>|...
    Finalizer trace. Standard C# does not guarantee lexical-scope finalization or finalizer order.
    The lifecycle section explicitly requests GC/finalizer draining after scoped allocations, but
    the parser should not impose ordering on FINALIZER records.

Major coverage
--------------
- async methods: void, Task, Task<T>, ValueTask, ValueTask<T>, custom task-like return type
- await: Task/ValueTask/custom awaiters/dynamic await/configure-await/suspension in conditions
- async lambdas, anonymous methods, local functions, method groups, delegates and events
- async streams, await foreach, cancellation-aware async streams, await using / IAsyncDisposable
- deliberate async faults before/after suspension, catch filters, rethrow, finally, aggregation
- CancellationTokenSource, linked cancellation, registrations and cancellation races
- Thread/ThreadStart/ParameterizedThreadStart, Start/Join, background threads, Interrupt/Yield/SpinWait
- ThreadPool work, unsafe queueing, registered waits and timer callbacks
- lock and Monitor Enter/Exit/TryEnter/Wait/PulseAll/reentrancy/exception release behavior
- Interlocked operations, MemoryBarrier, Volatile reads/writes and legal volatile field types
- ManualResetEvent, AutoResetEvent, ManualResetEventSlim, Semaphore, SemaphoreSlim
- CountdownEvent, Barrier, Mutex including abandoned mutex behavior, WaitAny/WaitAll/SignalAndWait
- ReaderWriterLockSlim and SpinLock
- Task.Run, StartNew, continuations, WhenAll/WhenAny, TCS, LongRunning, attached child tasks,
  nested Task<Task<T>> + Unwrap, synchronous Wait/Result/GetAwaiter().GetResult(), scheduler data
- Parallel.For/ForEach/Invoke including Break and Stop
- ConcurrentQueue/Stack/Bag/Dictionary and BlockingCollection
- SynchronizationContext, ExecutionContext, AsyncLocal<T>, ThreadLocal<T>, [ThreadStatic]
- intentional unsynchronized race versus Interlocked control
- constructors/finalizers/base constructor parameter flow and private/protected/public access from workers
- giant for -> while -> do -> if -> for -> while -> do -> switch -> try/catch/finally -> Task nesting
- awaited expressions inside complex boolean short-circuit conditions and loop conditions
- per-type for/while/do-while matrices for legal numeric/native/floating/decimal/char types,
  plus bool/string state loops
- switch statements and switch expressions across primitive, string, enum, object, dynamic,
  struct, record and array/list-pattern inputs
- constant, type/declaration, relational, logical, property, positional and list/slice patterns
- generic declarations and async generic methods for every requested arity:
    <T>
    <T, TResult>
    <T1, T2>
    <T1, T2, TResult>
    ...
    <T1, ..., T10>
    <T1, ..., T10, TResult>
- generic position matrix: 20 canonical concrete type categories rotated through every input slot
  at every arity 1..10, plus an independently rotated TResult slot (1300 position tests)
- generic constraints, new(), class/struct/unmanaged/notnull, static-abstract generic operators
- C# 11: >>> / >>>=, required/init, list patterns, raw strings, UTF-8 literals, generic attributes,
  auto-default structs, ref fields/scoped refs, checked user-defined operators, static abstract members
- unsafe pointer/address/dereference/stackalloc/function-pointer code executed from worker-thread tests
- nullable/coalescing/null-conditional, tuples/deconstruction, ranges/indices, anonymous types,
  iterator/yield/foreach, default interface methods, covariant returns, extension methods, partial types,
  named/optional/params arguments, CallerArgumentExpression, interpolated-string handlers,
  C# 10 lambda improvements, dynamic member dispatch, interpolation and nameof

Generic canonical type-position set
-----------------------------------
bool, byte, sbyte, short, ushort, int, uint, long, ulong, nint, nuint, char,
float, double, decimal, string, object, dynamic, SmallValue, WorkPayload.

Validation performed
--------------------
- delimiter/comment/string structural scan: balanced
- zero `using` directives detected
- global `printf(...)` calls retained
- no external source generator is required by the fixture itself

A stock Roslyn compile was not available in the generation environment. The source intentionally
assumes a global printf intrinsic, so normal Roslyn validation also requires adapting that intrinsic.
